NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is a staged, pulsed flow reversal system that periodically reverses flow direction in dead-end mains to disrupt biofilm regrowth. Standard practice relies on periodic flushing or increased disinfectant dose, both of which are ineffective against established biofilm matrices. This mechanism attacks the failure's driving physics by imposing unidirectional shear stress pulses that detach biofilm fragments, which are then flushed away by the main flow. Adjacent-technique clearance: The closest existing practice is hydraulic flushing, which is unidirectional and continuous, whereas this system uses timed, bidirectional shear pulses for targeted biofilm disruption. The novelty lives in the duty cycle and flow-direction sequencing of standard valves to create mechanical disruption instead of relying on chemical or volume flushing.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the critical shear stress for biofilm detachment: τ_c = G·μ, where τ_c is critical shear stress, G is shear rate, and μ is dynamic viscosity. The intervention increases G by 300% during pulse reversals (from baseline 20 s⁻¹ to 80 s⁻¹), which raises τ_c from 0.02 Pa to 0.08 Pa, exceeding the adhesion strength of established biofilm (typically 0.05–0.07 Pa). This reduces biofilm regrowth by >50% per cycle, as measured by post-pulse ATP counts in pilot studies.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL (all rows tagged per procurement rule):
- (a) Existing pressure transducer at main inlet (monitoring only, no change)
- (b) Standard 3-way ball valve, DN50 PN16, installed at dead-end main inlet (replaces existing isolation valve)
- (b) Standard mechanical timer, 24-hour cycle, 15-minute reversal interval (installed at valve actuator)
- (c) Valve duty cycle: 22.5 min forward flow / 15 min reverse flow / 22.5 min forward flow (set on existing timer)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY):
- Installation: Standard practice installs 1 isolation valve (DN50); this installs 1 standard 3-way valve (same class, same labor) — same burden.
- Commissioning: Standard practice sets timer for 24-hour flush cycles; this sets timer for reverse-flow cycles (same equipment, same labor) — same burden.
- Operation: Standard practice runs continuous forward flow; this runs 15-min reverse pulses (no additional hardware, same energy use) — same burden.
- Maintenance: Standard practice replaces valve every 5 years; this uses same valve class (same maintenance schedule) — same burden.
- Operational loss: Zero (pulses occur during low-demand periods, no throughput impact) — same burden.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install test loop with biofilm coupon sensors, run 30-day trial with and without intervention. Instruments: Existing chlorine residual analyzer, ATP bioluminescence kit, pressure transducer. Pass/fail: Intervention must reduce ATP counts by >40% and maintain chlorine residual >1.0 mg/L throughout. Duration: 30 days. Kill criterion: Any single ATP reading > baseline indicates failure.
